entry.title: What's (on) the menu?
entry.summary: A few months ago, I shared how I love to find inspiration when I browse other digital designers' websites. Another example of this is the navigation design for this website. As the site has gone through a few iterations, the navigation had gone from non-existent…
entry.content:
A few months ago, I shared how I love to find inspiration when I browse other digital designers' websites. Another example of this is the navigation design for this website.

As the site has gone through a few iterations, the navigation had gone from non-existent — because it was a one-page site — to a traditional menu drawer. From a UX perspective, I never loved the menu drawer. Aside from the technical and best practices issues, it bothered me that it didn't spark delight.

When I came across Dunstan Orchard's personal website, where the navigation is just one sentence with two options, I took his idea and ran with it.

My version is a bit more elaborate (my website's structure is more complex), but the way it works is: the header on each page has a sentence that tells you where you are and gives you a few options of where you can go next.

For example, on this page it says:

"You’re reading one of my posts. Get to know me, or explore my work instead."

and on the about page, it says

"This is the about page. You can find my resume here, read my posts, or explore my work."

While I acknowledge that this technically violates Jakob's Law, the trade-off is worth it here. The navigation is simple enough so this slightly out of left field design won't be too confusing. I'd even argue that it supports the purpose of this website — to give you some insight into who I am and how I work — better than a menu drawer would.

I hope you like it, and I hope Dunstan doesn't mind me riffing on his idea. You should check out his work. His reel-to-reel player is absolutely incredible.

entry.title: AKM Logo
entry.summary: My brother-in-law is an incredible interior design photographer. Over the years, I've had the pleasure of helping him out with his digital presence. Way back when, that included a custom WordPress website where I had the chance to experiment with atypical UI and IxD patterns…
entry.content:
My brother-in-law is an incredible interior design photographer. Over the years, I've had the pleasure of helping him out with his digital presence. Way back when, that included a custom WordPress website where I had the chance to experiment with atypical UI and IxD patterns (anyone remember "bottom of the window headers"?!). More about that in a future post.

Recently, Adam wanted to update his logo. The logo he was using was a simple lettermark that spelled "AKM".

As part of the refresh, we wanted to better match a photography business. The old logo read too much as a clothing or furniture brand. We also wanted it to explicitly communicate the business Adam is in.

I came up with 4 options. All have a full lockup that includes "Adam Kane Macchia Photography" and a square minimal companion logo. Macchia is emphasized in all 4 options. All are 1 color for maximal versatility.

Looking at these from top to bottom, here's how I think of them.

  • The first one takes cues from contemporary furniture companies. The Massimo Vignelli influence is clear.
  • The second option leans more mid-century modern and real-estate.
  • The script in the third option introduces a softer element and is inspired by Italian appliance logo designs.
  • The last option is classic, elegant, and has an editorial interior design feel.

Adam decided to go with the last option, but we used the lettermark from the script one. It adds visual interest and softens the look and feel.

For purely aesthetic reasons (and we all know aesthetics can't be argued about), my favorites were option 1 and 3. Both of those have an appliances or furniture logo feel though. So Adam was probably right to go with the one that reads most editorial — after all, that's where a lot of his work ends up.

I'm not a professional logo designer. But ever since I designed the logo for the youth tennis club I was a part of as a 12-year old, I've enjoyed creating the occasional logo. There are many facets and nuances to creating logos which makes each project a fun challenge.

entry.title: Moto Trip Report
entry.summary: When I used to live in Vermont, I'd ride my motorcycle any chance I got. One of my favorite rides was from where I lived in Montpelier down to my in-laws in Chester. I was worried that moving to Massachusetts would mean much less riding.
entry.content:
When I used to live in Vermont, I'd ride my motorcycle any chance I got. One of my favorite rides was from where I lived in Montpelier down to my in-laws in Chester. I was worried that moving to Massachusetts would mean much less riding. While this turned out to be true, I still have great riding roads close to home. And the ride to my in-laws — now heading north instead of south — is just as nice.

On these rides, I often think about how nice it would be to have my childhood friend along. We grew up riding BMX bikes and skateboards. And later in life, we both started riding motorcycles. We never get a chance to ride together though. He still lives in Belgium, and when I visit I obviously don't bring my bike along.

When I was there last, I floated the idea of a fall foliage trip up into Vermont. He was immediately interested and within a few weeks our plan was set. He'd fly to the US. We'd rent a bike for him. And we'd spend a few days riding northern Massachusetts and Vermont roads.

The trip was last week, and we had a blast. The leaves were just starting to turn. The weather was perfect for riding. And I enjoyed showing my friend around and spending some quality-time with him.

I'm already thinking about what our next adventure might be.

For now, it's back to work!

entry.title: Fun with footers?
entry.summary: A lot of what you see here can be traced back to an idea I had when I saw someone, do something, somewhere else. I guess that's the definition of being inspired. A while ago, I came across the personal website of Zoe Minikes. I pretty much love…
entry.content:
A lot of what you see here can be traced back to an idea I had when I saw someone, do something, somewhere else. I guess that's the definition of being inspired.

A while ago, I came across the personal website of Zoe Minikes. I pretty much love everything about it. The idea I ended up remixing is near the bottom of the page. A simple dynamically generated sentence in the footer: "It’s the [late afternoon] of the [fifteenth], and the digital sky is smiling on you."

So fun! I decided to take this idea and run with it. My version has the exact time of day and date spelled out in lowercase text. Instead of the static second part of the sentence, I created a bank of sentences or statements that are somewhat related to the time of day.

When someone comes across it in the footer, I hope it brings as much delight to them as Zoe's version did for me.

This post is tagged with "AI-assist" because I did need some help coding the widget. 😊

More updates inspired by my fellow digital designers to come soon!
